Health & Breathing Safety Notice

Last updated: September 15, 2026

BreathLever is an educational, general-wellness tool. It is not a medical device and does not provide medical advice, diagnosis, monitoring, treatment, rehabilitation, or emergency services. BreathLever is available only to users aged 18 and older.

Before you use a breathing practice

Ask a qualified healthcare professional before starting if you are pregnant, receiving medical or mental-health treatment, have recently had surgery, or have a history of fainting, seizures, panic triggered by breath focus, cardiovascular disease, high or low blood pressure, respiratory disease, or a neurological or eye condition. Do not change medication or a treatment plan because of information in the App.

Age and safety preferences are self-reported. Eligibility checks and risk labels do not establish medical suitability or detect an emergency. Keep your safety preferences accurate; if your health changes, review them before practicing. Use is also subject to the Terms of Use, including the capacity to agree under applicable law.

Older adults should start with short, comfortable practices without breath holds. Age alone does not determine whether a practice is suitable; health conditions, symptoms, treatment and personal comfort matter. If you are frail, have difficulty breathing or are unsure whether a method is suitable, seek individualized advice before starting.

Use a safe setting

Practice seated or lying down in a safe, well-ventilated place. Never practice while driving, operating machinery, in or near water, in a bath or shower, standing where a fall could cause injury, or after alcohol, drugs, or medication that impairs judgment. Do not combine the App with cold exposure or other hazardous activities.

Do not force breathing or breath holds

Keep every breath comfortable and smaller than your maximum. Breath-hold methods are distinct methods: removing a hold does not turn a named ratio such as 4–7–8 into the same practice. If a hold is uncomfortable or conflicts with your safety profile, stop that method and choose a separate no-hold practice.

Self-guided timers, including custom methods, limit each continuous breath hold to at most 10 seconds; some methods have stricter limits. This is a product limit, not a target, recommendation or medically established safe duration for you. In custom methods, 0 seconds means no hold. Never hold your breath to keep up with a timer. When you pause a session, return to normal breathing; do not continue holding.

Rapid, forceful, prolonged, connected, reduced-volume, carbon-dioxide-tolerance, and long-hold methods can cause hyperventilation, air hunger, tingling, panic, dizziness, fainting, or injury. BreathLever provides no self-guided timer for restricted methods. Their entries are limited to history, evidence limitations, risks, professional-guidance advice, and external references.

Stop and seek help

Stop immediately and return to normal breathing if you feel dizzy, faint, confused, numb, panicked, unusually short of breath, in pain, or otherwise unwell. Seek prompt medical advice if symptoms are new, worsening, or persistent. Call local emergency services for severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, loss of consciousness, signs of stroke, or any situation that may be immediately dangerous.

Evidence and results

Evidence varies by method and may be limited, preliminary, or apply only to supervised clinical populations. A cited article does not mean that BreathLever or the exact App timing has been clinically validated. No result is guaranteed, and general-wellness exercises must not be used to manage a diagnosed condition without appropriate clinical guidance.

External links and names

External links are provided for independent education. Third-party sites control their own content and terms. References do not imply sponsorship, affiliation, endorsement, or permission to reproduce a third party’s program. Method ideas and historical facts are described in original editorial language; third-party text, branding, recordings, and course materials remain the property of their respective owners.

Your choice

You may stop any practice at any time. If you do not understand or accept this notice, do not start a breathing session. Nothing in this notice excludes rights or responsibilities that cannot lawfully be excluded.
